subject: Post-demo: EdgeApp competitive cost model & next validation steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Daniel Li <daniel.li@edgeapp.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-21T14:08:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: EdgeApp competitive cost model & next validation steps

Hi Daniel — thanks again for the demo and for walking through the integration goals. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we can align the quantitative comparison you asked for.

Call recap (high level)
- EdgeApp is focused on low-latency chat at volume (~150k active monthly users, ~250 requests/s at peak simulations).
- Key success metrics: p95 latency < 300ms, cost per 1M tokens (inference only) target < $180, and cache hit >= 40% to hit unit economics.
- Current hyperscaler baseline: you shared the quote PDF (attached) showing managed endpoint costs and a per-request latency SLA.

What we recommend for a fair apples-to-apples evaluation
1) Token-econ run (1M token profile): we run a controlled 1M token job with: warm cache scenario, cold cache scenario, and a hybrid with your representative prompt/response size distribution. This shows realized token/unit cost with realistic KV cache hit rates.
2) Batching sensitivity: run three batching profiles (no batching, micro-batching 8, and aggressive batching 32) to show latency vs cost tradeoff and where Redwood's batching/runtime yields better pareto.
3) Latency SLO validation: p50/p95/p99 traces for the same load on Redwood Dedicated vs the hyperscaler endpoint (we'll mirror request arrival patterns you provided).
4) Canary plan: small traffic canary (1% production) for 48hrs with tracing headers so you can validate production behavior.

Data we need from you to configure tests (can be a short CSV)
- Typical prompt length (avg tokens), typical response length (avg tokens)
- Percent of requests you expect to be cacheable (by prefix or identical prompts)
- Expected concurrency patterns (peak RPS, sustained RPS)
- Any region constraints or egress concerns

Deliverables and timeline
- We’ll produce a token-econ workbook (attached: redwood_token-econ-runbook.xlsx) with modeled per-1M token costs across configurations.
- Tests (1)–(3) above: start provisioned tests by Fri 2026-10-23 if we get your data by EOD Thu 10/22.
- Final readout + recommendation doc by Mon 10/26.

Next steps (proposed)
- Can you share the sample CSV with token distributions and an internal contact for procurement? (Maya?)
- Approve provisioning window (we need a short ephemeral cluster for aggressive batching runs).

Attachments: redwood_token-econ-runbook.xlsx (xlsx), edgeapp_demo-recording.mp4 (mp4)

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben and Marissa for pricing and canary details.

Best,
Priyom Das
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
priyom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — developer-first inference for predictable latency & cost

Internal notes / ask: Ben, Marissa — forwarding Daniel's CSV and the hyperscaler quote. Key points for our pricing and test scoping: 

- They expect ~45% cacheable requests; that improves their unit-econ materially if we can show similar cache-hit in our test. Model both 35% and 50% scenarios.
- Peak RPS 320, sustained 140 — plan a canary at 1% traffic but run sustained load tests at 200RPS to validate p99 under load.
- Hyperscaler quote shows managed endpoint with per-inference markup and separate data egress; we should highlight Redwood dedicated per-token delta and where caching/batching reduces cost.

Suggested quick numbers to include in the workbook (we'll refine after tests):
- Redwood baseline (no cache, no batching): $225 per 1M tokens
- Redwood with caching (45% hit) + micro-batching 8: $155 per 1M tokens
- Hyperscaler managed endpoint (from their quote): $260 per 1M tokens (estimated, includes some infra fees)

Ask: Ben — can you produce a conservative pricing scenario (list + committed discount tiers) and a recommended canary config (instance types, max batch size, mem for KV cache) by EOD Thu 10/22 so we can provision? Marissa — can you pull any customer references that did heavy prefix caching?

Thanks,
Priyom
